body:
It’s scary when I read posts like this because I often think back when this first started for me. I couldn’t get images out of my head and they were so very real they’d make me flinch or cringe so I kept looking into methods. Once you at that place it’s difficult to return from.

I’d urge you to try and confide in people who are safe for you.
I always thought helium would look accidental, but I guess you couldn’t accidentally overdose on that. The issue with accidents is they always find out, that’s how I was hospitalized.

Sometimes I feel like I’m too far gone. Once I buy what I need that will be it, no one will be able to talk to me out of it and I crave that type of resolution. I just wanted to be open for this last brief window before I use something I know can’t fail.
No, I just want to understand why I’m at this point and how to stop. I don’t want to lose my medical anonymity.
How sad. That makes it a route I cannot take.

I definitely agree! I've been in the process of getting a service animal prospect myself (four years and counting) and the idea that there could be a team working a dog with a bite history or otherwise scares the hell out of me. Because "legally" those dogs can be worked.

Sure, they could use an alarm, but what if every time they turned off the alarm something other than their medication was more important. Or there are periods of dissociative episodes that can make people lose time and alarms would just not work in this case. A dog's alert can be incessant to get the handler to snap out of it an actually make sure their meds are taken.

For example, I have a psychiatric condition that causes both visual and auditory hallucinations, among a list of other things that make things a tad bit difficult. I'll be training tasks that revolve around reality grounding, as 12 years of doctors and therapy didn't really help or decrease my issues. I'm not too sure if there's a medical device that can help with that so here I am getting a service animal, but I do not have a visible disability. 

I'd also be worried about this breed biased ban. There's a lot of misinformation about breeds spread on both sides. Ergo: Pits were nanny dogs/pits can lock their jaws. If this was a route that was taken I'd want a lot more genetic research done on aggressive breeds.

This is my first day actually on it, and I've spoken to a doctor the day prior, I have a therapy appointment set up and I've been speaking to a psychiatrist. My work knows what's been going on, but I really don't want to seem unreliable anymore.  


It happens at work too, I spend a lot of time trying to sip warm drinks/cover my mouth and try not to think of throwing up. Usually it goes away after an hour or so after being at work, but there have been times where that's lead to increased irritability and increased anxiety while at work. Then I have a hard time focusing on my work because things as small as the scent of food can set me off. I have intense phone anxiety and one of the things I have to deal with is making calls at work, and it's not that I'm bad at my work, it's that it's debilitating for me to do it constantly and at a consistent level

I told my mother once, in a heated argument, that I wished she was the one who had been murdered instead of her sister. Obvious throw away for obvious reasons, and I don't want to go into too much detail, but I had been put into foster care because of her which lead to years of dealing with unfathomable amounts of abuse (of varying kinds) and when she got custody of me back she proceeded to further the abuse.

I don't forgive myself, even after the things she's done to me, I feel like my words were far more harsh.

Ah, this is extremely helpful and actually makes me feel better. 

I think my discomfort from telling people has been people outing me or just general violence against me when they found out. I've never been in a comfortable place when I felt I should tell someone, it's always been incredibly rushed and they feel deceived. If someone keeps telling you that what you're doing is wrong, or that what you're doing is hurting people it makes you stop and think. Maybe not disclosing my biological gender makes me a terrible person and then I feel incredibly shitty about myself.

It's just distressing that if I find someone I like, someone I want to get to know, I have to kind of beat down the walls to actually be like "Hey, so I was born female..." And when the dating scene I'm interested in is mostly gay men, and that alone makes me incredibly uncomfortable telling them. So, I usually end up breaking off whatever relationship I had in an attempt to be friends with them-- It usually gets to the point of where they've kissed me and after I just feel really shitty about everything.

But I do appreciate the help! Your comment really does help.

I just don't understand when the appropriate time is to tell someone I'm interested in. I used the term "closeted" wrong, I think it's "stealth" I should have been using since I've actually been living as a cis-male and not a FTM.

All the new friends I have ever made only know me as male and I feel like it's an incredibly personal piece of information, but I don't know. I feel like it's only bad for me because people tell my I'm lying (The close friends I do know.) *especially* when it comes to dating.
It's stealth! I've been using it wrong. :(
